A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MGPS research and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Added material can be distinguished from renumbered or relocated content.

before.justification: v1 reports original Gaussian simulations, FFHQ/ImageNet reconstruction experiments, and PTB-XL ECG imputation and diagnosis results in Section 4 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds 1,000-image evaluations and additional image-quality results in Tables 7–10.

M1.justification: The midpoint decomposition, Gaussian variational objective, optimization, warm-start strategy, and latent-space procedure are retained. Algorithm 1 replaces an explicit Gaussian sampling formula with equivalent kernel notation. New Appendix C.3 analyzes a restricted case without changing the proposed sampler.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Gaussian problems, FFHQ/ImageNet image tasks, and PTB-XL missing-block and missing-lead tasks. The larger evaluation reuses five existing image tasks and three existing priors; it expands sample size rather than dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The original comparator sets remain. The added 1,000-image study selects subsets: its half-mask comparison includes DDNM/DiffPIR, while latent comparisons include ReSample without PSLD. Further apparent changes are uncertain: Table 7 labels motion and nonlinear comparisons DDNM/DiffPIR despite the restrictions stated in Section 4 and Appendix D.2.

E3.justification: v1 evaluates image reconstruction on 50 images per dataset using LPIPS. v2 retains this evaluation and adds 1,000-image comparisons on five tasks across three priors, with FID and additional PSNR/SSIM evaluation. Appendix B.2 also corrects the stated Wasserstein-2 formula, without establishing that the Gaussian experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: The midpoint-fraction and gradient-step ablations, diffusion-step comparisons, runtime/memory analysis, and reconstruction examples are retained. The larger benchmark evaluation and additional metrics do not introduce a separate ablation, robustness test, or case study.

E5.justification: Table 7 newly reports confidence intervals for image LPIPS, PSNR, and SSIM, whereas v1's image tables report means only. Their construction and confidence level are unspecified. Existing Gaussian-mixture replication information and ECG uncertainty reporting remain unchanged; no increase in repeated runs is documented.

E6.justification: Original Tables 1–5 and matched appendix LPIPS values are unchanged. v2 adds extensive PSNR/SSIM results and 1,000-image estimates including FID in Tables 7–10. For example, latent HDR FID is 44.2 for MGPS versus 38.7 for ReSample. These are newly reported results, not same-setting performance improvements over v1.

T1.justification: New Appendix C.3 derives differences between a one-step, fixed-covariance MGPS case and DPS; C.1 supplies a derivation of the existing KL bound. B.2 restores the missing factor 2 in the Gaussian Wasserstein formula, and Section 2 adds the missing noise-variance factor to the DPS weight. The central midpoint lemma and proof are retained.

C1.justification: The core contributions remain the midpoint decomposition and variational posterior sampler, with competitive image reconstruction and ECG applications. The abstract and introduction emphasize public health more strongly, but describe the same ECG reconstruction and diagnosis contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix D.6 newly explains uneven baseline reconstructions through ImageNet diversity and half-mask difficulty. D.4 interprets the larger evaluation as confirming earlier findings, and Section 4 adds wearable-device motivation. Existing limitations concerning midpoint selection, guidance cost, and warm-start instability remain.

D1.justification: The abstract and Section 4 newly state that MGPS experiment code is public and provide its repository location. v1 provides competitor links but no corresponding MGPS access information. Existing hyperparameters, ECG architecture, preprocessing, and training-time disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Liu et al. (2023), Seshadri et al. (2020), and Van Erven and Harremos (2014) for reconstruction context, wearable diagnosis motivation, and the KL argument. Appendix C.3 explicitly distinguishes MGPS from DPS. The broader positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the midpoint explanation, replaces potential notation g with likelihood notation throughout much of the text, reorganizes image-evaluation paragraphs, and expands ECG motivation. Author contribution and correspondence text and several appendix headings change, while the overall section structure remains.

P2.justification: v2 adds the midpoint diagram and Tables 7 and 10, expands the former LPIPS-only Tables 7–8 into multimetric Tables 8–9 with ranking highlights, and relocates ECG tables and figures. It also corrects the reversed left/right caption of the Gaussian plot. The reconstruction images themselves are retained.

improvement.justification: The broader metric reporting, larger image evaluation, mathematical corrections, DPS comparison, and code-access information improve transparency and explanatory support. These gains are limited by Table 7's contradictory comparator labels, Table 8's PGDM JPEG SSIM entry of 12.76, and D.4's blanket superiority interpretation despite Table 7 exceptions. The original evidence remains intact, supporting a limited net improvement.
